subject.title: fix(chutes): add timeouts to OAuth HTTP requests

question: Should Chutes OAuth token and userinfo HTTP requests fail after the new 30s request deadline by default?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but the default changes existing auth behavior from unbounded network waits to fail-closed OAuth HTTP requests for very slow token or userinfo responses.

options.title: Accept bounded auth requests
options.body: Land the 30s default because it prevents indefinite Chutes login hangs and follows the shared OAuth request-signal pattern.

options.title: Tune the deadline first
options.body: Ask for a different Chutes-specific timeout while keeping the same helper and regression tests.

options.title: Pause for live provider evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers see provider-specific Chutes OAuth latency evidence for the chosen deadline.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded auth requests
recommendation.body: Land the 30s default because it prevents indefinite Chutes login hangs and follows the shared OAuth request-signal pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Chutes OAuth and shared OAuth helper history makes this the best available routing owner for the auth-boundary tradeoff.
